title: With Midterms Approaching, Trump Implores Republicans: Pretend I’m on the Ballot!
content: President Trump was in South Carolina to stump for Darline Graham, sister of Lindsey. But his own political future was on his mind, too.

title: Postal Service Publishes Finalized Plan to Restrict Mail Ballots
content: The plan complies with President Trump’s executive order to restrict mail voting, which was blocked by federal courts and is under review at the Supreme Court.

title: Judge Strikes Down Trump’s 75-Country Visa Ban
content: The ruling from the Southern District of New York found that the policy went beyond Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s legal authority.

title: Alfalfa Sprouts Linked to Illnesses in 15 States, F.D.A. Says
content: Officials are investigating after multiple strains of E. coli and a type of salmonella sickened dozens of people across the United States. Two people were infected with both salmonella and E. coli.

title: Trump Accounts Get an Unlikely Endorser: Gavin Newsom
content: Mr. Newsom, the governor of California, normally has harsh words for President Trump. But he called the new children’s savings accounts “one of the best things” the president has done.

title: Drawing on His Rust Belt Roots, Vance Campaigns for Republicans
content: Vice President JD Vance traveled to his hometown, Middletown, Ohio, and spoke at a steel factory where his grandfather once worked.

title: Pentagon Fires Editor and Publisher of Independent Military Publication
content: The firings at Stars and Stripes also claimed a Middle East correspondent. They are the latest effort by the Pentagon to diminish the news outlet’s editorial independence.

title: Defense Rests Case in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial
content: The two sides focused Friday on whether Ms. Clancy was experiencing psychosis when she strangled her three young children in 2023. Closing arguments could begin on Monday.

title: Court Slashes Award Alex Jones Was Ordered to Pay Sandy Hook Parents
content: An appeals court reduced the award to the parents of one victim to $6 million from $49 million, citing a Texas damages cap. The conspiracy theorist owes over $1 billion in other cases.

title: America Ends a Summer of Lightning-Fast Primaries and Political Speed Dating
content: Plot twists in several states have led to rapid-fire races that have felt more reminiscent of European-style snap campaigns than traditional American marathons.

title: Massachusetts’ Top Court Bars Statues of Catholic Saints at City Building
content: The ruling quashes a plan by the mayor of Quincy that had drawn opposition from many religious figures, as well as from residents of the racially diverse city.

title: U.S. Agreed to Pay Liberia $5 Million in Connection with Deportees, Documents Say
content: The Trump administration approved the payment after Liberia said it would consider taking migrants from other countries.

title: Desperation Mounts as Thousands in Indiana Endure 10 Days Without Power
content: Floods from powerful thunderstorms devastated Gary, where a third of residents live below the poverty line and full restoration isn’t expected until next week.

title: Small Plane Crashes in Western Alaska, Killing Eight
content: The Cessna aircraft was carrying two pilots, two U.S. Army engineers and four contractors to Cape Newenham from Anchorage when it crashed near a U.S. military site, investigators said.

title: Prison Firm Donated to Trump’s PAC After ICE Gave It $165 Million a Year in Contracts
content: The GEO Group has profited from the administration’s mass deportation campaign. A subsidiary donated more than $1.4 million to the president’s super PAC last month.

title: Chief Justice Allows Trump to Continue White House Ballroom Construction, for Now
content: The 90,000-square-foot ballroom project has grown in size and scope, with the president’s lawyers saying it is intertwined with the renovation of an underground military bunker.

title: The Local: Drama in the Boundary Waters
content: William Kent Krueger talks about his thriller set in the Boundary Waters, a timely subject.

title: Guide Company That Ran Fatal Ski Trip Faces Safety Fine in California
content: The state levied a $151,300 fine on Blackbird Mountain Guides, which took backcountry skiers into the Sierra Nevada in threatening conditions. Nine died in an avalanche.

title: Gazebos From Uzbekistan: The Latest Foreign Gifts in Trump’s Washington
content: The structures will go up in West Potomac Park, the site of President Trump’s planned National Garden of American Heroes.

title: Trump Threatens Defamation Suit Over National Guard Report, Aiming to Intimidate a Critic
content: It was the latest example of President Trump’s bid to use the legal system against those who voice unflattering facts and opinions generally protected by the First Amendment.

title: Push for Online Gun Sales Meets a Surprising Opponent: Small Gun Dealers
content: The Trump administration wants average Americans to be able to buy guns online and have them shipped to their doors. Small gun stores warn it could upend the industry and risk public safety.

title: U.S. Citizen Who Deleted Phone’s Data Says His Prosecution Puts Privacy at Risk
content: Samuel Tunick, who faces a felony charge for deleting his phone’s data during an airport customs search, called the government’s peering into people’s private lives “creepy.”

title: He Said He Was the World’s Healthiest Man. Then Came a Stunning Diagnosis.
content: Bryan Johnson, the longevity guru, wants to live forever. But the big question is why.

title: How Harvard’s Epic Fight With Trump Is Costing the University
content: The federal government has slowed Harvard’s funding, despite the university’s legal victories. The conflict is forcing hard choices on campus.

title: Texas governor calls for Justice Dept. probe of Muslim washing stations
content: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott escalated his campaign against Muslim washing stations at the state’s major airports.

title: Government will cut water to Ariz., Calif., Nevada as Colorado River runs low
content: The states must curb their use of water from the river starting in 2027.

title: White House space policy directs agencies to send humans to Mars
content: A new space transportation policy from the Trump administration calls for a dramatic increase in launches, as well as working with the commercial space industry to send humans to Mars.

title: Democrats remain far behind GOP in cash on hand as midterms near
content: New filings find the Democratic National Committee trailing its Republican counterpart by more than $100 million, with millions of dollars in debts.

title: Why this U.S. state is trying to ban ‘addictive’ social media features to protect teens
content: Advocates say legislation in the nation’s most populous state would carry particular weight in the national movement to curb tech’s influence on young people.

title: Inside the police investigation into how Rep. Max Miller’s daughter got hurt
content: Video recordings and documents detail how investigators pursued the case, and the possibility of abuse, for months but failed to identify a perpetrator.

title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott takes aim at Muslim washing stations in airports
content: Legal experts dispute Abbott’s claims that the ritual washing stations are discriminatory, with some saying his attack fits a pattern of anti-Muslim actions and rhetoric.

title: These 5 People Spent Decades Behind Bars. Here Are Their Stories.
content: Francis Clifford Smith, who died at 101, was among the longest-incarcerated people in the U.S. Here are some others who lived much of their lives in prison.

title: Frank Smith, Who Served 70 Years for Murder, Dies at 101
content: One of the longest-serving prisoners in American history, he was sent to death row in 1950 before his sentence was commuted to life imprisonment.

title: For Some in a Disrupted D.C., Grand Prix Is More Irritation Than Celebration
content: Race preparations have snarled traffic, rerouted flights and forced the National Gallery of Art to conduct vibration tests.

title: Police Chief in Mississippi Regularly Used Racist Slurs, Private Text Messages Reveal
content: Text exchanges obtained by reporters show troubling messages sent by the chief of a Mississippi police department facing an uproar over the fatal shooting of a 1-year-old boy in June.

title: How a Progressive Democrat in Florida Gave Her Party New Hope — and New Fears
content: Angie Nixon, a state lawmaker from Jacksonville, shocked Democrats in red Florida by soundly defeating her centrist primary opponent. Now comes the hard part.

title: Harry and Meghan See Their California Dreams, and Riches, Fade Away
content: Like so many others before them, Prince Harry and Meghan arrived in Hollywood with big plans. They are leaving with their star power fading.

title: In Ohio, Haitians Feel Shaken by Ankle Monitors and Increased ICE Presence
content: The devices, which will make it easier for authorities to locate immigrants in Springfield if large-scale deportations begin, have intensified a sense of dread.

title: Why Polling Chaos Could Create Big Problems for American Politics
content: Bad polls. Misleading betting odds. Surveys meant to shape narratives. Ahead of the midterms and 2028, there is suddenly serious confusion about candidate strength and voter sentiment.

title: How the Billionaire Joe Lonsdale Shaped Trump’s Homelessness Policy
content: As Republicans have embraced tough measures to clear the streets, no group has led the way more than the Cicero Institute, founded by the venture capitalist Joe Lonsdale.

title: Why the Lindsay Clancy Case Is Dividing Americans
content: She is being tried on murder charges for killing her three young children. The tragedy has resurrected debates over whether such women are criminals or victims.

title: She set aside the fiddle to raise nine children. At 99, she made her Opry debut.
content: Violet Hensley, who has died at 109, was one of the last links to a bygone era of foot-stomping American folk music.

title: Ten days after storm, thousands are still waiting for power in Indiana
content: Residents are scrambling for generators, lining up for gas and bracing for a long recovery.
